questions.question: Is the area free of trash, materials, and other debris on the ground?
Are there enough trash cans around the area?
Are the trash cans emptied often enough that they don't pile up or spill?
Are walking and working areas clear of slip and trip hazards like trash, standing water, ice, or mud?
Are materials and tools stored properly: on dunnage, steel on 6x6 dunnage, and pipe and rolling stock chocked?
Is the lighting adequate for the work?
Do conditions call for carbon monoxide monitoring?

follow_up.Yes: What's being done to monitor and reduce carbon monoxide?

questions.question: Is anyone working 6 feet or more above a lower level, including in aerial lifts?

follow_up.Yes: What type of work, and where?

questions.question: Are elevation changes of 19 inches or more protected with a ramp, stairs, warning line, or other means?
Are all open holes 2 inches or larger covered, secured, and signed?
Are guard rails and cables set up properly: top rail at 42 inches plus or minus 3, mid rail, toe board, 200 pound rating, and 3 cable clamps?
Are any scaffolds in use, with signed inspection tags and used properly?
Are aerial lifts in use by people with training on file?

follow_up.Yes: About how many aerial lifts are on site?

questions.question: Are all aerial lifts inspected before use each day?
Is anyone using personal fall arrest gear, and is it inspected and fitted properly?
Is the fall protection equipment right for the situation?
Are any cranes in use?

follow_up.Yes: How many, what are they doing, and where?

questions.question: Are all crane inspections up to date?
Does each crane have a controlled access zone for the swing radius and load?
Is all other equipment inspected each day and free of leaks or damage?
Do operators have training certificates on file and stickers on their helmets?
Are operators of mobile equipment wearing seatbelts?
Does all mobile equipment have working backup alarms, horns, lights, mirrors, and signals?
Does all mobile equipment have a fire extinguisher the operator can reach?
Are aerial lifts used on firm, level ground with crush protection over the controls?
Are fire extinguishers staged properly: at each stair landing, 25 to 75 feet from flammable storage, within 100 feet of any work, and on all mobile equipment?
Are all fire extinguishers inspected monthly and tagged as current?
Are all flammable materials stored in the right places?
Are flammable storage areas protected from vehicles, with an extinguisher 25 to 75 feet away, No Smoking signs, and no ignition sources?
Are flammable storage cabinets grounded and within capacity?
Do fuel storage areas have secondary and spill containment?
Are all cords in good shape with GFCI protection at the power source?
Are extension cords in good shape, raised at least 7 feet on non-conductive supports, or rolled up when not in use?
Are all cords marked with this month's inspection color?
Are construction power skids marked, protected, and clear for 36 inches on all sides?
Is all live electrical equipment, including electrical rooms, labeled with identification and warnings?
Is there a LOTO program with Controlling and Authorizing Energy Marshals and a central LOTO station?
Are all tools used properly with safeguards in place and working?
Are all knives on site the automatic self-retracting type?
Is material secured when saws and grinders are used?
Are all hand-held bandsaws on site dual-trigger?
Do all drills with a half inch or larger chuck, except hammer drills, have auto-stop or anti-rotation?
